article.title: Morning Soundings: Tension Wood, Food Bills, and Survivor Authority

capture.notes: Captured during the publication run from sources accessed on September 9, 2026, after checking the same-day Save Point edition and coverage ledger for overlap.

signals.headline: A tree can straighten without knowing which way is up

canonicalSubject.name: Proprioception-driven tension wood formation in hybrid poplars

signals.canonicalClaim: A controlled experiment on young Populus tremula × alba stems found that curvature sensing redirected tension wood to the convex side and actively straightened stems when directional gravity and light cues were suppressed.
knownFacts: The experiment used young hybrid poplars in spherical chambers with light arriving evenly from all directions.
A clinostat rotated bent stems to suspend useful gravitropic sensing after upward curvature had developed.
During subsequent straightening, tension wood formation stopped on the former upper side and appeared on the convex side.
The authors report a curvature-dependent control law balancing proprioceptive and gravitropic feedback.
uncertainties: The cellular and molecular mechanism by which the stem senses its curvature remains unknown.
The study does not establish that the same tissue response operates identically across tree species and life stages.
The controlled chamber does not reproduce every mechanical and environmental load experienced by mature trees.

evidence.notes: The peer-reviewed open-access paper reports the experimental setup, anatomical evidence, and control-law analysis; the INRAE release provides an accessible institutional account from the participating research organization.

sources.title: Proprioception drives tension wood formation for autotropic straightening and postural control in trees
A newly discovered role for tension wood: the muscle trees use to correct their posture

openQuestions: Which cells and molecular pathways convert stem curvature into redirected tension wood formation?
How widely does the measured control law generalize across tree species and mature stems?
How do wind, branch loading, damage, and changing light interact with proprioceptive feedback in the field?

watchFor.trigger: A follow-up identifies or experimentally tests the cellular or molecular mechanism responsible for curvature sensing.
A study reproduces active tension-wood straightening under suppressed gravity and light cues in another woody species.

disposition.reason: The result establishes a controllable phenomenon while leaving a specific molecular sensor and cross-species scope open to later evidence.

signals.selectionReason: The experiment turns a familiar tree movement into a concrete feedback-control problem and reveals wood as both structure and actuator.

signals.headline: The regional average has no food bill

canonicalSubject.name: Income-resolved multisector resource security scenario ensemble

signals.canonicalClaim: An exploratory ensemble of 3,735 multisector scenarios found that projected food and residential-energy burdens can vary sharply across income deciles within the same modeled region, so regional averages conceal distributional risk.
knownFacts: The study used version 7.1 of the Global Change Analysis Model across 32 geopolitical regions, 235 water basins, and 384 land-use regions.
The ensemble varied 12 factors and analyzed 3,735 scenarios through 2050.
For food and residential-energy burdens, each region was divided into ten equal-population income groups.
One modeled southern Africa outcome placed food burden at 49.6 percent of income for the poorest decile and 5.5 percent for the richest decile.
uncertainties: The ensemble does not assign probabilities or identify one most likely future.
Its results depend on model structure, baseline data, and the range of assumptions selected by the researchers.
Income-resolved estimates inside large regions do not capture every local market, household strategy, or political intervention.

evidence.notes: The open-access peer-reviewed paper documents the scenario design and burden estimates; MIT News provides an institutional explanation based on the paper and author interviews.

sources.title: Identifying Key Uncertainties and Drivers of Future Resource Security Outcomes Through a Multisector Scenario Ensemble
Study predicts large disparities in access to food, water, and energy in 2050

openQuestions: Which model assumptions most strongly determine the distribution of food and energy burdens within each region?
How closely can income-decile burden estimates be validated against household-level observations?
Which policy interventions reduce burden for low-income groups without shifting insecurity into another resource system?

watchFor.trigger: A follow-up compares the modeled income-specific burdens with household or subnational data in a named region.
Researchers use the ensemble to test a specific food, energy, water, trade, or income policy across distributional groups.

trackingTerms: Gi Joo Kim resource security ensemble

disposition.reason: The study is worth preserving as a methodological reference, but it names no near-term milestone and future value depends on region-specific validation or application.

signals.selectionReason: The study shows that aggregation is not neutral when the phenomenon of interest is household access rather than total resource supply.

signals.headline: The record changes when Survivors frame it

canonicalSubject.name: Stolen Childhoods exhibition about the Mohawk Institute

signals.canonicalClaim: The Survivor-created Stolen Childhoods exhibition opened at the Royal Ontario Museum on September 8, combining archival records, photographs, interviews, and sculpture with visitor provisions shaped around Indigenous Survivors.
knownFacts: The exhibition was created by the Survivors' Secretariat with support from Know History and Museums Assistance Program funding.
Its materials include archival records, photographs, multimedia interviews, a seven-foot sculpture, and portraits of eight Survivors by Nadya Kwandibens.
ROM held a dedicated private viewing for Indigenous visitors, organizations, and Survivors before the public opening.
The installation includes a dedicated Indigenous reflection space with sacred medicines and is scheduled at ROM through October 1, 2026.
The Survivors' Secretariat also describes a mobile version intended for schools, events, and smaller institutions.
uncertainties: The sources reviewed are from the exhibition's creators and host institution rather than independent critical assessment.
Future venues and the long-term preservation of the installation were not established during this capture.
An exhibition can broaden public knowledge but does not by itself resolve questions of records access, investigation, commemoration, or accountability.

evidence.notes: The factual description comes from the Survivor-led creator and the Royal Ontario Museum as host; no independent exhibition review was identified at the time of capture.

openQuestions: Where will the traveling and mobile versions be shown after the ROM engagement?
How will Survivor authority over the material be maintained as the exhibition moves between institutions?
Will the exhibition's interviews and digital timeline remain publicly accessible after the physical installations close?

watchFor.trigger: The Survivors' Secretariat announces a new venue or tour schedule for Stolen Childhoods.
The creators announce a durable digital archive, educational release, or preservation plan for the exhibition materials.

trackingTerms: Nadya Kwandibens Mohawk Institute Survivor portraits

disposition.reason: The exhibition is explicitly designed to travel, with future venues and the stewardship of Survivor-authored materials observable over time.

signals.selectionReason: The exhibition makes authorship part of historical method by allowing Survivors to determine how institutional records and lived testimony meet the public.
